privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.lead: {{brand}} collects only what an order needs: your name, phone number, delivery address, email and order history. Card details are handled by our payment gateway and never reach our servers. We share your address with delivery partners only, and never sell your data to anyone.

controller.title: Who is responsible for your data
controller.body: {{brand}} operates this online store and is responsible for the personal information collected through it. For any question about this policy, or to exercise any of the rights described below, write to us at {{email}}.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: To create an account and deliver an order we collect your name, phone number, email address and delivery address. We keep a record of what you have ordered. If you contact support we keep that correspondence. We also record basic technical information such as your device type and the pages you visited, which is what tells us the site is working.

payment.title: Payments
payment.body: Card and mobile wallet payments are processed by our payment gateway. Your card number, PIN and one-time codes are entered on the gateway's own page and are never sent to, stored by, or visible to {{brand}}. We receive only a confirmation that a payment succeeded or failed. Cash on delivery involves no payment data at all.

sharing.title: Who we share it with
sharing.body: Your name, phone number and address go to the courier carrying your parcel, because otherwise it cannot be delivered. Our payment gateway, email provider and SMS provider each receive only what their part of the job requires. We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for anyone else's advertising.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: We use cookies and browser storage to keep you signed in, to remember your cart and wishlist between visits, and to remember the language you chose. Clearing your browser storage removes all of it, and the store still works without it — you will simply start with an empty cart.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Order records are kept for as long as we need them for accounting and for handling returns or disputes. Account details are kept until you ask us to delete your account. Support conversations are kept while they are useful for helping you.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.body: You can ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you, correct anything that is wrong, or ask us to delete your account. Marketing emails and push notifications are off unless you turn them on, and you can turn them off again at any time from your profile.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: Write to {{email}} with any privacy question or request, and we will respond as quickly as we can.

whatIsKoreanRamen.question: What is Korean ramen?
whatIsKoreanRamen.answer: Korean ramen, or ramyun, is an instant noodle made with a chewier, springier noodle than Japanese ramen and a soup base that is usually spicy. It cooks in about five minutes in boiling water and is eaten as a full meal rather than a side.

leastSpicyRamen.question: Which Korean noodles are least spicy?
leastSpicyRamen.answer: Mild options include jjajang (black bean) and creamy carbonara-style noodles, which have little to no chilli. Shin Ramyun sits in the middle, and Buldak varieties are the hottest — the 2x and 3x versions are considerably hotter than the original.

ramenVsRamyun.question: What is the difference between ramen and ramyun?
ramenVsRamyun.answer: Ramen is the Japanese dish, usually fresh noodles in a long-simmered broth. Ramyun is the Korean instant version: pre-fried noodles with a powdered soup base, spicier and quicker to cook. Most packets sold in Bangladesh are ramyun.

cookRamen.question: How do I cook Korean ramen?
cookRamen.answer: Boil about 550 ml of water, add the noodles and the soup sachets, and cook for four to five minutes, stirring. For stir-fried types like Buldak, drain most of the water before stirring the sauce through. An egg or sliced cheese takes the edge off the heat.

bibigoHalal.question: Is Bibigo mandu halal?
bibigoHalal.answer: The Bibigo products {{brand}} imports are halal certified. Bibigo makes both pork and non-pork lines worldwide, so check the packaging of the specific item — the ones stocked here are from the certified range.

storeMandu.question: How should I store mandu and dumplings?
storeMandu.answer: Keep them frozen until you cook them, and cook straight from frozen without thawing. Thawing first makes the wrappers soggy and they tear. Once cooked, eat them the same day rather than refreezing.

cookMandu.question: How do I cook Bibigo mandu?
cookMandu.answer: Pan-fry from frozen in a little oil for two minutes, add a splash of water, cover, and steam for six to seven minutes until the water has gone. They can also be steamed for about ten minutes or air-fried at 180°C.

sushiAtHome.question: What do I need to make sushi at home?
sushiAtHome.answer: Four essentials: short-grain sushi rice, nori seaweed sheets, rice vinegar for seasoning the rice, and soy sauce. A bamboo rolling mat and wasabi are worth adding. Raw fish is optional — vegetable and cooked fillings work just as well.

sushiRice.question: Can I use normal rice for sushi?
sushiRice.answer: Not really. Sushi needs a short-grain rice whose starch makes the grains cling together, so a roll holds its shape. Long-grain rice such as basmati stays separate and the roll falls apart when you cut it.

storeNori.question: How do I keep nori crisp?
storeNori.answer: Keep it sealed and dry. Nori absorbs moisture from the air within hours of opening and turns limp, so reseal the pack with the silica sachet inside. Limp sheets crisp up again if passed briefly over a low flame.

drinkMixes.question: How do I prepare Tang and Rooh Afza?
drinkMixes.answer: Tang is a powder: stir about two tablespoons into a glass of cold water. Rooh Afza is a syrup: pour two tablespoons into a glass and top with chilled water or milk. Both are popular for iftar and keep well once opened.

snacksShelfLife.question: How long do the snacks stay fresh?
snacksShelfLife.answer: Every pack carries its own printed expiry date, and {{brand}} ships stock well inside it. Store unopened packs somewhere cool and dry, and finish an opened pack within a few days — humidity is what makes them go soft here.
